request.system: You are an experiment designer for a fraud ranking model. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Propose 3 or 4 distinct configurations to test next with 5-fold cross-validation. Each must differ meaningfully (model family, feature set, imbalance handling or capacity). You only see cross-validation results; the test set is hidden from you. You can preview a configuration on 3 CV folds before including it in your batch. Use the preview to filter out bad configs and only propose ones that show promise. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

tools.name: get_fold_preview
tools.description: Run a proposed model config on 3 CV folds to preview performance before committing to full 25-fold CV. Returns mean PR-AUC and standard deviation.

output.text:
I previewed four configurations on 3 CV folds each. All four look promising enough to include in the 5-fold batch. The previews are noisy, with a standard deviation of 0.04 to 0.08 across folds. The gaps between configs are about the same size as that noise, so the ranking is tentative.

| # | Model | Features | Imbalance | Params | Preview PR-AUC | SD | Precision at top 50 |
|---|-------|----------|-----------|--------|----------------|----|---------------------|
| 1 | LightGBM | all (63) | none | num_leaves 15, 300 trees, learning rate 0.03 | 0.722 | 0.084 | 0.787 |
| 2 | LightGBM | no_size (50) | class_weight | num_leaves 7, 200 trees, learning rate 0.05 | 0.685 | 0.068 | 0.767 |
| 3 | Random forest | no_size (50) | class_weight | 500 trees, min_samples_leaf 3 | 0.664 | 0.082 | 0.733 |
| 4 | Logistic regression | all (63) | class_weight | C 0.3 | 0.663 | 0.036 | 0.733 |

- **Config 1** is the lead candidate. It has the highest PR-AUC and the best precision at the top of the ranking, which matters because the audit queue is only about 100 providers.
- **Config 2** is a smaller LightGBM with no size features. Comparing it with config 1 tests whether dropping the size features costs much accuracy. Size features may mostly capture provider volume, which says little about fraud itself.
- **Config 3** is a different model family. It adds diversity and could be useful in an ensemble.
- **Config 4** is a simple, stable baseline. It has the lowest fold variance, and it shows how much the tree models gain from nonlinearity.

I did not preview SMOTE or the agent feature sets, so they are untested. The `agent` feature set has 0 features, so I skipped the `+agent` options.

The labels are only a measure of suspicion, so a high PR-AUC means the model reproduces whoever flagged these providers. It does not show that the model finds confirmed fraud.
